chicken-drumstick-baked-or-broiled-skin-.title: Chicken drumstick, baked or broiled, skin not eaten

content.title: About
content.content: Skinless chicken drumstick prepared by baking or broiling in a fast‑food/restaurant setting. The meat is tender and relatively low in fat when the skin is omitted. Often served as a single portion in combo meals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken drumsticks contain more iron than breast meat because of the darker muscle.
Baking without skin reduces calories by roughly 30 % compared with skin‑on versions.
Fast‑food chains frequently marinate drumsticks beforehand to speed up cooking.
Drumsticks are commonly paired with dipping sauces, enhancing their appeal.
Internal temperature should reach 165 °F (74 °C) for safe consumption.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Skinless drumstick provides about 20 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Removing the skin cuts saturated fat content, which is beneficial for heart health.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains niacin (B3) and vitamin B6, important for energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Contains minerals
items.content: Provides phosphorus, selenium and zinc, which support bone health and immunity.

items.title: Promotes satiety
items.content: The high protein level helps you feel full longer after a meal.

items.title: Food‑borne illness risk
items.content: Undercooked chicken may harbor salmonella; ensure proper cooking temperature.

items.title: Chicken allergy
items.content: A small number of people can be allergic to chicken proteins.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Restaurant preparations often add salt and sauces, increasing sodium intake.

items.title: High glycemic impact of sauces
items.content: Sweet dipping sauces can cause rapid blood‑sugar spikes.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Eat the drumstick by pulling the meat off the bone with your hands. Serve with vegetable sides, fries, or a salad. Sauces are optional, but watch the amount of added salt.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cool cooked drumsticks to 4 °C within 2 hours and keep refrigerated for up to 24 hours. For longer storage, freeze in an airtight bag for up to 3 months; thaw in the refrigerator before reheating.

coffee-instant-decaffeinated-pre-lighten.title: Instant Decaffeinated Coffee, Pre‑lightened and Pre‑sweetened with Low‑Calorie Sweetener, Ready to Reconstitute

content.title: About
content.content: This instant decaffeinated coffee is made from selected beans that undergo decaffeination, pre‑lightening and the addition of a low‑calorie sweetener. After drying and granulation the product is ready to be reconstituted with hot water.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Decaffeination is usually performed by water‑process or CO₂ extraction, preserving most flavor compounds.
Pre‑lightening reduces bitterness and yields a smoother taste.
Low‑calorie sweeteners such as stevia or erythritol provide sweetness without added sugar.
Instant coffee retains up to 70 % of the original brew’s aromatic compounds.
Packaging often comes in single‑serve sachets, ideal for travel and office use.

items.title: Low caffeine content
items.content: The absence of caffeine makes it suitable for people sensitive to stimulants.

items.title: Supports hydration
items.content: Reconstituting with hot water helps maintain the body’s fluid balance.

items.title: Low‑calorie sweetener
items.content: Stevia and erythritol contribute virtually no calories, aiding energy‑balance control.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Coffee contains polyphenols that provide antioxidant activity even after processing.

items.title: Convenience and time saving
items.content: Quick preparation without grinding beans saves time in a busy schedule.

items.title: Coffee allergy
items.content: A small number of individuals may experience allergic reactions to coffee components.

items.title: Additive content
items.content: Some low‑calorie sweeteners can cause gastrointestinal discomfort in large amounts.

items.title: Loss of aroma compounds
items.content: Drying and granulation reduce the amount of aromatic substances compared with freshly ground coffee.

content.title: How to Prepare
content.content: Add one sachet (≈2 g) to hot water (80‑90 °C) and stir for 30‑60 seconds. Optionally add milk, cream, or spices such as cinnamon or cardamom.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place in a tightly sealed package, protected from moisture and direct sunlight. Shelf life is typically 12‑24 months.

content.title: About
content.content: Perch (NFS) is a freshwater fish from the Percidae family, found in rivers and lakes across Europe and Asia. It has light, firm flesh with a mild flavor, low fat content, and high nutritional value. Perch is commonly prepared baked, fried, or boiled.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Perch can grow up to 60 cm in length and weigh more than 3 kg.
In the wild, perch prefers cold, clear waters with good oxygen levels.
In Russia, perch is considered a delicacy and is often served in upscale restaurants.
Perch meat is rich in omega‑3 fatty acids, which are beneficial for heart health.
Perch can change the color of its skin depending on lighting and mood.

items.title: Rich in omega‑3
items.content: Perch provides EPA and DHA omega‑3 fatty acids that support cardiovascular health.

items.title: High-quality protein
items.content: The flesh supplies all essential amino acids needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Low fat content
items.content: Compared with many other fish, perch contains relatively little fat, making it suitable for diet-conscious eating.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Perch is a good source of B12, B6, and niacin, which aid nerve function and metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: It also provides phosphorus, selenium, and iodine, important for bones, immunity, and thyroid function.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to perch.

items.title: Heavy‑metal contamination
items.content: In certain water bodies perch can accumulate mercury and other toxins; purchase from reputable sources.

items.title: Potential parasites
items.content: Raw or undercooked fish may contain parasites; ensure thorough cooking.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Perch can be baked with herbs, pan‑fried, steamed, or boiled in broth. Fillets work well in salads, soups, and pastas. For a milder taste, the fish is often marinated in lemon juice and olive oil before cooking.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Fresh perch should be kept in the refrigerator at 0‑2 °C, wrapped in plastic, and used within 2 days. Frozen perch can be stored at –18 °C for 3‑4 months. Thaw in the fridge rather than at room temperature.

content.title: About
content.content: Freezer pop is a frozen dessert pop – a flavored ice lollipop on a stick. It is made from water, sugar, fruit or berry concentrates and sometimes a small amount of dairy. The product is popular as a refreshing treat in hot weather.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Freezer pop originated in the United States in the 1960s and quickly became a summer favorite.
It often contains natural fruit extracts, giving it a bright and intense flavor.
The stick format makes it easy to eat on the go.
There are many flavor variations: strawberry, lemon, watermelon, mango, and more.
Freezer pop is frequently used in culinary shows to create “icy” visual effects.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: The high water content helps maintain fluid balance, especially in warm conditions.

items.title: Low Fat Content
items.content: Unlike traditional ice cream, frozen pops contain virtually no fat.

items.title: Source of Vitamin C
items.content: Fruit concentrates can provide a modest amount of vitamin C, supporting immunity.

items.title: Moderate Sugar Levels
items.content: Sugar content is generally lower than in non‑frozen candies, making it a less calorie‑dense snack.

items.title: Easy Digestion
items.content: The frozen form melts slowly, which can be gentler on the digestive system.

items.title: Allergy to Fruit Ingredients
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to the fruit extracts used.

items.title: Sugar Content
items.content: Despite being moderate, the product still contains sugar and can affect blood glucose levels.

items.title: Risk of Frostbite
items.content: Prolonged contact with the frozen pop may cause mild frostbite of the oral mucosa.

items.title: Not Suitable for Young Children
items.content: Because of the stick and solid form, there is a choking hazard for small children.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Freezer pop is typically served frozen, held by the stick, and allowed to melt slowly in the mouth. It can be stored in the freezer for up to 6 months. It can also be added to drinks or used as a garnish for desserts.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep Freezer pop in an airtight container in the freezer at –18 °C (0 °F) or lower. Avoid prolonged exposure at room temperature to prevent melting and loss of texture.

content.title: About
content.content: Lau lau is a traditional Thai dessert consisting of steamed sticky‑rice dumplings filled with sweet mung‑bean paste or coconut shreds. The treat has a soft, chewy texture and a subtle aroma from the steaming process.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Lau lau is commonly sold at street stalls and markets throughout Thailand.
Traditionally it is steamed in bamboo baskets, which imparts a unique fragrance.
Regional variations use different fillings such as mango, pumpkin, or sweet beans.
The name "lau lau" comes from the Thai word meaning “to steam”.
Vegetarian and vegan versions are available, made without eggs or dairy.

items.title: Rich in complex carbohydrates
items.content: Sticky rice provides a steady release of energy and helps keep you feeling full.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Traditional Lau lau is steamed without added oil, making it a light dessert.

items.title: Contains plant protein
items.content: Bean‑based fillings add protein that supports muscle maintenance.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Beans and whole grains aid healthy digestion.

items.title: B‑vitamin content
items.content: Mung beans supply B1, B2 and B6 vitamins, which are important for metabolism.

items.title: Soy allergy
items.content: Some fillings may contain soy sauce or soy protein.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Sticky rice can raise blood sugar quickly, so people with diabetes should consume it in moderation.

items.title: Contamination risk from street vendors
items.content: Improper storage can lead to bacterial growth; choose reputable sellers.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Lau lau is served hot, often drizzled with sweet coconut sauce or paired with a light soy dip. It can be enjoyed as a standalone snack or alongside fresh fruit and tea.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked Lau lau in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. For longer storage, freeze them in a separate bag; re‑steam before serving.

stuffed-tomato-with-rice-and-meat.title: Stuffed Tomato with Rice and Meat

content.title: About
content.content: Stuffed tomato with rice and meat is a classic dish consisting of a ripe tomato filled with a mixture of boiled rice, ground meat (usually beef or pork), onion and spices. The tomato is baked until tender, resulting in a fragrant and hearty meal.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The dish is popular in Mediterranean, Balkan and Middle Eastern cuisines.
Traditionally the tomato interior is scooped out and the flesh is used in sauces or soups.
Some regional versions add pine nuts or raisins for a subtle sweet note.
Stuffed tomatoes are often served as part of festive tables or family lunches.
A lighter version replaces meat with chicken or turkey.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Meat and rice provide B12, B6 and niacin, which support metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Good source of protein
items.content: Ground beef or pork supplies complete animal protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Lycopene in tomatoes
items.content: Tomatoes are high in lycopene, a powerful antioxidant that promotes heart health and may reduce the risk of certain cancers.

items.title: Complex carbohydrates
items.content: Rice offers slow‑releasing energy, helping to maintain satiety.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: The dish contains iron, zinc and potassium, important for blood formation, immunity and blood‑pressure regulation.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Using ready‑made sauces or adding excess salt can make the dish too salty, which is undesirable for hypertension.

items.title: Meat fat content
items.content: Fatty cuts of beef or pork increase calories and saturated fat; choosing lean cuts is recommended.

items.title: Tomato allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to tomatoes, experiencing skin rashes or food‑related reactions.

items.title: Thorough cooking required
items.content: Undercooked ground meat may harbor pathogens; ensure the internal temperature reaches at least 71 °C.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the stuffed tomato hot, often accompanied by a fresh vegetable side, yogurt‑based sauce, or a green salad. It can be enjoyed as a main course or as part of a larger meal.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cooked stuffed tomatoes keep in the refrigerator in an airtight container for up to 3 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑size bags for up to 2 months. Reheat thoroughly before serving.

content.title: About
content.content: The Whopper Jr with cheese is a smaller version of Burger King’s classic Whopper, topped with melted cheese. It includes a 71 g beef patty, sesame seed bun, a slice of processed cheese, pickles, fresh tomato, lettuce, onion and the signature sauce. Served hot and ready to eat.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The Whopper Jr was first introduced in the 1990s as a compact alternative to the original Whopper.
The cheese used is typically a processed American cheese that melts in seconds.
Although often part of kids’ combo meals, the burger is popular with adults looking for a smaller portion.
In several countries Burger King offers local twists on the Whopper Jr, adding bacon or regional spices.
The Whopper Jr with cheese contains roughly 340 kcal, making it less caloric than the full‑size Whopper.

items.title: Protein
items.content: The beef patty provides about 14 g of protein, essential for muscle repair and satiety.

items.title: Iron
items.content: Red meat is a good source of heme iron, which is readily absorbed by the body.

items.title: Calcium from cheese
items.content: The melted cheese adds a modest amount of calcium, supporting bone health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Meat and the bun contain B6 and B12 vitamins, important for nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Dietary fiber from vegetables
items.content: Tomato, lettuce and onion contribute a small amount of fiber that aids digestion.

items.title: High sodium
items.content: The sauce and cheese can add a notable amount of salt, which may be a concern for hypertension.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: Beef and processed cheese contain saturated fats that, in excess, can raise cholesterol levels.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: Cheese contains dairy proteins and the bun contains gluten; individuals with allergies should be cautious.

items.title: Caloric content
items.content: Despite its smaller size, the burger still provides about 340 kcal, which can affect daily energy balance.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The Whopper Jr with cheese is designed to be eaten by hand. It can be split in half for smaller bites or topped with extra sauce to taste. It pairs well with fries and a cold beverage.

content.title: Storage
content.content: The burger is best consumed immediately after preparation. If needed, store it in the refrigerator for up to 2 hours, wrapped in foil or plastic wrap to retain moisture. Reheat in a microwave for 30‑40 seconds or in an oven at 150 °C.
